native_mechanisms: Bone-colored die-stone (accumulator) is never reset between marks — every fold carries the callus of all prior folds
Each mark's weight is pressed into the stone's already-turned seat (add-in, quarter-turn, multiply), so earlier marks bend how later marks land — strictly order-dependent, serially chained state
Only the stone's final seated position against the wooden keeps is emitted; all intermediate turns/residue are swept away and discarded
Fold count equals mark count regardless of pile length — constant per-mark work, streaming over arbitrarily long input
Avalanche claim: a hair's-width change is multiplied by each successive fold so no two differing paths converge on the same last step
core_technique: xxHash64 verbatim: four parallel 64-bit accumulator lanes seeded with the golden-ratio primes, each running acc = rotl31(acc + w*P2) * P1 over 32/64-byte blocks, lane merge via rotl(1,7,12,18) + four round-and-keep steps, length add, 8/4/1-byte tail rounds, and the xor-shift/multiply avalanche finalizer — i.e. exactly the known multiply-xor-rotate accumulator fold, with multi-lane ILP as a generic textbook optimisation not derived from the single-stone image.
